incident-bot: Page triggered for high error rate on Quasar (enterprise VPC - dedpool-qsr-01). 
incident-bot: Metric: model_response_5xx_rate > 3% for 5m, latency p95 spiking. Affected models: quasar-llama-3-13b & quasar-llama-3-13b-quant. Severity: P2.
maya-oncall: I'm on it, paging handoff to maya-oncall. @sam.sre can you join?
sam.sre: joining now. seeing 502 spikes from the dedpool gateway, looks correlated with KV cache warming after a rollout?
liam.eng: I see increased memory pressure on the GPUs in dedpool-qsr-01, OOM-ish logs for the quant variant. Pulling logs.
liam.eng: log snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T10:03:12Z] model-server: allocation failed: requested 132MB > available 120MB
[2026-03-15T10:03:12Z] fallback: attempt to route to safe-variant quasar-llama-3-13b-safe-v1
```
maya-oncall: Quasar (customer) explicitly requested no noisy fallbacks last quarter — they want controlled switchovers. Nina, can you loop in Quasar SRE to confirm mitigation path?
nina.cs: pinged quasar-sre (on call) and raised ticket QSR-4871. Quasar SRE says they prefer pin to a tested safe variant rather than automatic fallback.
quasar-sre: confirmed — we want traffic pinned to quasar-llama-3-13b-safe-v1 on dedpool-qsr-01, not a global fallback. Please coordinate maintenance window if possible.
maya-oncall: Plan: 1) Isolate dedpool-qsr-01 from new rollout traffic. 2) Pin tenant routing to safe variant version on that pool. 3) Monitor error rate for 15m. 4) Rollback or scale if needed. Need eng approval for the pin + short outage window.
sam.sre: Agreed. We can apply per-tenant override via routes API. Minimal churn if we do a live route update. Command to apply: ```bash
# pin tenant quasar to safe variant on dedpool-qsr-01
redwoodctl routes update --tenant quasar --pool dedpool-qsr-01 --model quasar-llama-3-13b-safe-v1 --duration 60m --reason "emergency pin during degradation"
```
liam.eng: Before we do that, suggest also draining new warm-up requests to reduce memory churn: set pool concurrency to 2 temporarily. ```bash
redwoodctl pool update dedpool-qsr-01 --concurrency 2```
This should reduce OOM frequency.
oliver-ops: I'll run the concurrency change and then the route pin. Doing concurrency change now.
oliver-ops: concurrency update succeeded. API now returning 200.
maya-oncall: OK proceeding with route pin in 2m, will notify Quasar and start 15m monitor. @quasar-sre we'll keep you in thread.
quasar-sre: Thanks, standing by.
pagerduty: Reminder: if pin causes >5% degraded requests, escalate to SE manager and consider burst to dedicated backup pool.
sam.sre: route pin executed: ```
redwoodctl: route update accepted -> id=rt-9832
```
maya-oncall: Monitoring window started @1976543300. Current 5xx: 0.9% (down from 3.7%). latency p95: 410ms -> 380ms.
quasar-sre: seeing reduced errors on our end as well. Good to proceed with 60m pin.
liam.eng: Memory pressure trending down, no further OOMs in last 3 mins.
maya-oncall: Leaving pin for 60m, but we'll be ready to rollback if metrics worsen. Follow-up actions: - create post-incident ticket with root cause hypothesis (quant variant kernel selection + cache warmup). - schedule a model vetting with Quasar for safe-variant cert. - add an automatic alert to detect pool warmup OOMs earlier.
nina.cs: Created QSR-4871-incident-log with links: https://redwood.console/incidents/QSR-4871 and convo logged.
sam.sre: tagging engineering follow-up: ENG-2432 (kernel memory accounting).
maya-oncall: Thanks all. I'll hand this off to oliver-ops for observability watch and sam for root cause. If anyone sees new spikes, ping @maya-oncall and escalate. :thumbsup:
quasar-sre: Appreciate the quick coord, will loop our platform team.
maya-oncall: thread closed for active work; will reopen if metrics degrade. last check @1976543899: 5xx=0.6%, p95=375ms.
